The test image shows close-up soybean stems/petioles with dark reddish-brown to purplish-brown discoloration streaking along the stems. Green pods are visible in the background. No obvious white mold, pustules, or leaf lesions visible. The dark stem discoloration with hairy stems is the key feature.

Top candidates: Anthracnose, Diaporthe, Phytophthora, Tobacco_Streak_Virus. Let me view reference images.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image key features:**
- Close-up of soybean stems/petioles showing dark reddish-brown to purplish-brown discoloration streaking along the stem length
- Green pods still present in background (actively growing plant)
- Hairy soybean stems typical of the species
- No white mold, no discrete pustules, no leaf lesions visible

**Comparison with candidates:**
- **Anthracnose**: Matches well — dark reddish-brown lesions on stems and petioles; black acervuli not visible here but could be early/mid stage
- **Diaporthe**: Shows distinct black pycnidia in linear rows — not clearly visible in test image
- **Phytophthora**: Typically shows stem discoloration at soil line with wilted dead plants — not matching
- **Tobacco Streak Virus**: Shows node streaks but primarily pod/leaf symptoms — not matching
- **Septoria/Cercospora**: Leaf diseases primarily — not matching this stem-focused image

The dark reddish-brown stem and petiole discoloration on an actively growing plant with green pods is most consistent with **Anthracnose**, which specifically causes dark irregular lesions on stems, petioles, and pods.
